trust_decision.summary: Decides whether a raw embedding-provider error term (which may carry the API key, request URL and provider response body) can be put into a caller-facing changeset error message; at the pinned commit the manual Vectorize change inspects it straight into the message.

landing_point.why: The summary names the 'vectorize change'; AshAi.Changes.Vectorize is the only place where inspect(error) goes into an error message, and the grep for the embedding 'generate(' call lands here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public Ash action :ash_ai_update_embeddings, defined by the transformer for the :manual and :ash_oban vectorize strategies (lib/ash_ai/transformers/vectorize.ex:76-124). Callers reach it through a code interface (test/support/music.ex:106), an Oban trigger job, or any AshAi tool/MCP or JSON:API exposure of that action.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix touches only lib/ash_ai/changes/vectorize.ex. The sibling implementation is untouched and is recorded as an O8 route instead.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: VectorizeAfterAction does not build a message. It only passes {:error, error} back from an after_action hook (lib/ash_ai/changes/vectorize_after_action.ex:59-60), so a solver can argue that it 'doesn't format anything' and that the report is about the manual strategy's message.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The error must still be attached to the vectorized fields and must still contain the stable text 'An error occurred while generating embeddings' (the fix's test asserts this). The successful path, change_attributes with the zipped vectors, must keep working. An over-broad fix that swallows the error, or returns {:ok} without embeddings, would break callers and the Oban retry semantics.

O6_input_shapes: arbitrary error term returned by an EmbeddingModel.generate/2 implementation (map or struct carrying request headers/URL/response body)
string error from the ReqLLM adapter's unexpected-response branch, which itself inlines inspect(other) (lib/ash_ai/embedding_models/req_llm.ex:73)

O7_producer.where: The error is produced by the pluggable embedding model (lib/ash_ai/embedding_model.ex:17; lib/ash_ai/embedding_models/req_llm.ex:57-73). It is an adapter, not a schema, serializer or cache, and the check (the formatting site) does call it directly.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The :after_action vectorize strategy calls embedding_model.generate in a separate change and returns the raw provider error term unchanged from the create/update after_action hook, so Ash surfaces it to the caller of the ordinary create/update action.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different strategy and module. It never builds a message string itself, so 'no inspect, no leak' looks plausible. The report and the fix talk about the manual vectorize change's error message.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same directory (lib/ash_ai/changes/), separate file. It is reached through regular create/update actions on a resource with strategy :after_action (lib/ash_ai/transformers/vectorize.ex:68-74), not through :ash_ai_update_embeddings.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The ReqLLM embedding adapter inlines inspect() of an unexpected ReqLLM.embed response into the error string it returns. That string then reaches whichever change formats or returns it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It only fires on a contract violation by ReqLLM ('unexpected response'), so it can be argued to be unreachable or a lower-level adapter detail.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Another directory (lib/ash_ai/embedding_models/), one hop below the change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Have the after_action strategy wrap the error as Ash.Changeset.add_error / InvalidChanges with a message containing inspect(error), mirroring vectorize.ex:51.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The two changes are near-duplicates, and a maintainer harmonising the error handling across strategies would copy the manual strategy's message.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Have the adapter normalise provider errors to a string such as "Embedding request failed: #{inspect(error)}" (a lower-level producer of the leaked text).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adapter already does this for the unexpected-response branch at line 73, so extending it to the error branch is a natural refactor. It also creates a producer the check never sees.

O9_family: CWE-209 sensitive information (credentials) in user-facing error messages

services: PostgreSQL (AshPostgres test repo; vectorization requires AshPostgres, lib/ash_ai/transformers/vectorize.ex:30-32; pgvector extension likely)
O10_build.project_tests: test/vectorize_test.exs (after_action, manual, ash_oban strategies, lines 12-74) with the stub AshAi.Test.EmbeddingModel in test/support/embedding_model.ex; resources in test/support/artist.ex

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace inspect(error) in vectorize.ex:51 with a generic message (plus a server-side Logger call) and stop, leaving VectorizeAfterAction returning the raw provider term.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/ash_ai.ex:504 raises 'Something went wrong' with inspect(error); this is unrelated to embeddings and was not pursued.
lib/ash_ai/mcp/server.ex:669 returns inspect(error) of a JSON parse error in a JSON-RPC response; this is a different sink and was not pursued.
lib/ash_ai/actions/prompt.ex:277 puts inspect(reason) of a tool-loop failure into an action error; this is the LLM-provider sibling of the same weakness but outside the vectorize scope.
unverified: Whether Ash (not vendored; no deps/ in the tree) renders a non-exception {:error, map} from an after_action hook as Ash.Error.Unknown.UnknownError with inspect(term) in its message. This determines how visible the O8 after_action route is to direct callers.

Through the AshAi tool/MCP formatter, an UnknownError has no specific ToToolError impl (lib/ash_ai/to_tool_error.ex:145-150 covers only the class structs), so the after_action leak may be masked as 'unexpected error occurred' on that surface. It would still be exposed to direct action callers, forms and JSON:API depending on their error handling.
Whether the add_error at vectorize.ex:49-52 becomes InvalidAttribute or InvalidChanges; both return error.message verbatim to tool callers (lib/ash_ai/to_tool_error.ex:39-49).
Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell). lib/ has about 42 .ex files, so it is assumed well under 5 MB of source.
Presence in the latest release: none given, so unknown.
